=== Economics ===
{{See also|Air pollution in Turkey#Economics}}

[[File:Co2-emissions-and-gdp.png|thumb|Recent economic growth emits less carbon dioxide]]

During the late 20th and early 21st centuries, growth of the [[Economy of Turkey|Turkish economy]], and to a lesser extent population, caused increased emissions from electricity generation,<ref name="rep4">{{cite report |url=https://unfccc.int/documents/271050 |title=Turkey's fourth biennial report |date=December 2019 |work=[[Ministry of Environment and Urban Planning (Turkey)|Ministry of Environment and Urban Planning]]}}</ref>{{Rp|10,11}} industry and construction,<ref name="CAT2019">{{cite report |url=https://climateactiontracker.org/documents/672/CAT_2019-11-29_ScalingUp_TURKEY_FullReport_ENG.pdf |title=Scaling Up Climate Action series: Turkey |year=2019 |publisher=Climate Action Tracker}}</ref>{{Rp|59–62}} as described by the [[Environmental Kuznets curve|environmental Kuznets curve hypothesis]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kılavuz |first1=Emine |last2=Dogan |first2=Ibrahim |date=August 2020 |title=Economic growth, openness, industry and CO<sub>2</sub> modelling: are regulatory policies important in Turkish economies? |url=http://ikt.nny.edu.tr/files/files/haber/2019-2020/ek2020.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210417023008/http://ikt.nny.edu.tr/files/files/haber/2019-2020/ek2020.pdf |archive-date=17 April 2021 |access-date=21 December 2020 |publisher=[[Nuh Naci Yazgan University]]}}</ref> And from the 1990s to the 2010s they were correlated with electricity generation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sevgül Bakaya |first1=Melahat |last2=Ağbulut |first2=Ümit |date=20 February 2021 |title=Electricity production based forecasting of greenhouse gas emissions in Turkey with deep learning, support vector machine and artificial neural network algorithms |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0959652620353695 |journal=Journal of Cleaner Production |language=en |volume=285 |bibcode=2021JCPro.28525324B |doi=10.1016/j.jclepro.2020.125324 |hdl=20.500.12684/10125 |issn=0959-6526 |s2cid=229424723 |url-access=subscription |hdl-access=free |article-number=125324}}</ref> But during the 2010s [[economic growth]] and the increase in emissions decoupled somewhat.<ref name="OECD2021" />{{Rp|59}} Since the 1970s the energy intensity of economic growth has fluctuated around 1&nbsp;kWh per 2011 USD,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Energy intensity |url=https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/energy-intensity |access-date=2022-04-01 |website=Our World in Data}}</ref> whereas the carbon intensity of energy has fallen from 300g per kWh to 200g per kWh.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carbon intensity of energy production |url=https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/co2-per-unit-energy |access-date=2022-04-01 |website=Our World in Data}}</ref> Carbon Tracker says that it is possible to [[Eco-economic decoupling|decouple]] economic growth and emissions, by expanding the country's renewable-energy capacity and investing in energy efficiency with a sustainable energy policy.<ref name="CAT2019" />{{Rp|63}}

On average the consumption-based CO<sub>2</sub> emissions of one of the richest 10% of people in Turkey is more than double that of someone in the rest of the population,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Beuret |first=Nicholas |title=Emissions inequality: there is a gulf between global rich and poor |url=https://theconversation.com/emissions-inequality-there-is-a-gulf-between-global-rich-and-poor-113804 |access-date=17 August 2021 |work=[[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]] |language=en}}</ref> as richer people tend to fly more.<ref>{{cite web |date=23 September 2020 |title=Confronting carbon inequality |url=https://www.oxfam.org/en/research/confronting-carbon-inequality |access-date=17 August 2021 |website=[[Oxfam#Oxfam International|Oxfam International]] |language=en}}</ref> Turkey's high [[income inequality]] may cause higher CO<sub>2</sub> emissions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=THE NEXUS BETWEEN INCOME INEQUALITY AND CO2 EMISSIONS: EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE FROM TÜRKİYE |url=https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/6256284}}</ref>

The long-term strategy says that public procurement will prioritize low-carbon products and services.<ref name=":55" />{{Rp|location=section 4.2.2.1}} Turkey has received climate finance from the [[Global Environment Facility]], the [[Clean Technology Fund]], and various bilateral funding, but is not eligible for the [[Green Climate Fund]] because of its status as a [[developed country]] under the UNFCCC.<ref name=":10" />{{Rp|43}}

Worldwide, [[marginal abatement cost]] studies show that improving the energy efficiency of buildings and replacing fossil fuelled power plants with renewables are usually the most cost-effective ways of reducing carbon emissions.<ref>{{Cite news |date=22 February 2021 |title=What is the cheapest way to cut carbon? |url=https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2021/02/22/what-is-the-cheapest-way-to-cut-carbon |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210321093414/https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2021/02/22/what-is-the-cheapest-way-to-cut-carbon |archive-date=21 March 2021 |access-date=21 March 2021 |newspaper=[[The Economist]] |issn=0013-0613}}</ref> A 2020 study said that the electricity sector is key, and that low cost abatement is possible in the building sector.<ref name=":19">{{cite report |url=http://www.lowcarbonturkey.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/LCDTR_Marginal-Abatement-Cost-Curves.pdf |title=Technical Assistance for Developed Analytical Basis for Formulating Strategies and Actions Towards Low Carbon Development |last=Raptsun |first=Mykola |access-date=21 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920165058/http://www.lowcarbonturkey.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/LCDTR_Marginal-Abatement-Cost-Curves.pdf |archive-date=20 September 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref> The same study said that low levels of abatement in agriculture would be cheap, but high levels very expensive.<ref name=":19" /> A 2021 study by Shura said that energy transition could increase national income by more than 1%, the largest part being wage increases due to higher skilled jobs,<ref name=":36">{{Cite web |title=Socioeconomic Impact of the Power System Transition in Turkey • SHURA Enerji Dönüşümü Merkezi |url=https://www.shura.org.tr/socioeconomic_impact_of_the_power_system_transition_in_turkey/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210917182806/https://www.shura.org.tr/socioeconomic_impact_of_the_power_system_transition_in_turkey/ |archive-date=17 September 2021 |access-date=19 September 2021 |website=SHURA Enerji Dönüşümü Merkezi |language=en-US}}</ref>{{Rp|8}} such as in wind and solar power.<ref name=":36" />{{Rp|58}} According to the study socioeconomic benefits, such as better health and wages, would be three times the financial cost.<ref name=":36" />{{Rp|15}}

Turkey's [[social cost of carbon|carbon emissions]] are costly, even without carbon tariffs from other countries.<ref>{{cite news |last=Nuccitelli |first=Dana |date=1 October 2018 |title=New study finds incredibly high carbon pollution costs – especially for the US and India |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/climate-consensus-97-per-cent/2018/oct/01/new-study-finds-incredibly-high-carbon-pollution-costs-especially-for-the-us-and-india |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190208114443/https://www.theguardian.com/environment/climate-consensus-97-per-cent/2018/oct/01/new-study-finds-incredibly-high-carbon-pollution-costs-especially-for-the-us-and-india |archive-date=8 February 2019 |access-date=24 February 2019 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The short-term health [[co-benefits of climate change mitigation]] have been estimated at $800&nbsp;million for Turkey in the year 2028 alone.<ref name=":21" />{{Rp|6}} Investment in green energy is far smaller than the country's potential.<ref name=":47">{{Cite web |date=4 March 2022 |title=Turkey balks at coal phaseout amid growing energy woes - Al-Monitor: The Pulse of the Middle East |url=https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2022/03/turkey-balks-coal-phaseout-amid-growing-energy-woes |access-date=2022-03-09 |website=www.al-monitor.com |language=en}}</ref> Academics have estimated that if Turkey and other countries invested in accordance with the [[Paris Agreement]], Turkey would break even around 2060.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wei |first1=Yi-Ming |last2=Han |first2=Rong |last3=Wang |first3=Ce |last4=Yu |first4=Biying |last5=Liang |first5=Qiao-Mei |last6=Yuan |first6=Xiao-Chen |last7=Chang |first7=Junjie |last8=Zhao |first8=Qingyu |last9=Liao |first9=Hua |last10=Tang |first10=Baojun |last11=Yan |first11=Jinyue |date=14 April 2020 |title=Self-preservation strategy for approaching global warming targets in the post-Paris Agreement era |journal=[[Nature Communications]] |volume=11 |issue=1 |page=1624 |bibcode=2020NatCo..11.1624W |doi=10.1038/s41467-020-15453-z |pmc=7156390 |pmid=32286257 |doi-access=free}}</ref>{{Rp|figure 4}} A 2023 IMF working paper says that carbon pricing can be designed to support poor people.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imf.org/-/media/Files/Publications/WP/2023/English/wpiea2023108-print-pdf.ashx|title=Climate Mitigation Policy in Türkiye}}</ref>

==== Fossil fuel subsidies ====
According to the OECD, [[fossil fuel subsidies]] in 2019 totalled over 25&nbsp;billion lira (US${{To USD round|25|TUR|year=2019|sf=2}}&nbsp;billion),<ref>{{cite web |title=Fossil Fuel Support – TUR |url=https://stats.oecd.org/Index.aspx?DataSetCode=FFS_TUR |website=[[OECD]]}}</ref> nearly 1% of GDP.<ref name=":36" />{{Rp|74}} Economics professor Ebru Voyvoda has criticised growth policies based on the construction and real estate sectors, and said that moving from fossil fuels to electricity is important.<ref name=":28">{{cite web |last=Voyvoda |first=Ebru |date=22 May 2021 |title=A country outside of the global climate policy: Turkey |url=http://www.observatoireturquie.fr/a-country-outside-of-the-global-climate-policy-turkey/ |access-date=28 May 2021 |website=Observatoire de la Turquie contemporaine}}</ref> According to a 2020 report by the [[International Institute for Sustainable Development]]: "Turkey also lacks transparency and continues to provide support for coal production and fossil fuel use, predominantly by foregoing tax revenue and providing [[state-owned enterprise]] investment."<ref>{{cite web |last=Geddes |first=Anna |display-authors=et al |date=9 November 2020 |title=Doubling Back and Doubling Down: G20 scorecard on fossil fuel funding |url=https://www.iisd.org/system/files/2020-11/g20-scorecard-turkey.pdf |website=[[International Institute for Sustainable Development]]}}</ref> A MWh of electricity from Turkish lignite emits over a tonne of {{CO2}}. Some electricity from these power stations is purchased by [[Electricity Generation Company (Turkey)|the state electricity company]] at a guaranteed price of US$50–55/MWh until the end of 2027,<ref name=":10" />{{Rp|176}} despite coal power subsidies being economically irrational.<ref name=":28" /> Coal miners' wages are subsidised.<ref name=":10" />{{Rp|178}}

The Petroleum Market Law provides incentives for investors to explore for oil and produce it.<ref name="difiglio" />{{Rp|198}} According to the OECD, in 2019 the fuel tax exemption for [[Petroleum naphtha|naphtha]], [[petroleum coke]] and [[Bitumen|petroleum bitumen]] was a subsidy of 6.7&nbsp;billion lira (US${{To USD round|6.7|TUR|year=2019|sf=2}}&nbsp;billion), the largest of Turkey's fossil fuel subsidies that year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fossil Fuel Support – TUR |url=https://stats.oecd.org/Index.aspx?DataSetCode=FFS_TUR |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112004527/https://stats.oecd.org/Index.aspx?DataSetCode=FFS_TUR |archive-date=12 November 2020 |access-date=28 November 2020 |website=[[OECD]]}}</ref> Petcoke is used in cement production.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Petcoke Podcast: Turkey's cement sector in 2020 |url=https://www.argusmedia.com/en/blog/2020/september/14/podcast-the-petcoke-podcast-turkeys-cement-sector-in-2020 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201207041215/https://www.argusmedia.com/en/blog/2020/september/14/podcast-the-petcoke-podcast-turkeys-cement-sector-in-2020 |archive-date=7 December 2020 |access-date=28 November 2020 |website=[[Argus Media]]}}</ref> In other countries fossil fuel subsidies have been successfully scrapped by good communication from government, immediate cash transfers to poor people, energy price smoothing and energy transition support for households and firms.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Rentschler |first1=Jun |last2=Bazilian |first2=Morgan |date=1 January 2017 |title=Policy Monitor—Principles for Designing Effective Fossil Fuel Subsidy Reforms |journal=Review of Environmental Economics and Policy |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=138–155 |doi=10.1093/reep/rew016 |issn=1750-6816 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=3 essential steps towards ending fossil fuel subsidies |url=https://www.weforum.org/agenda/2021/07/3-essential-steps-towards-ending-fossil-fuel-subsidies/ |access-date=19 September 2021 |website=World Economic Forum |language=en}}</ref>

== Politics ==
[[File:202406 Peoples' Climate Vote 2024 - UNDP.svg|thumb|Chart showing results of the Peoples' Climate Vote 2024 survey, regarding support for a quick transition away from fossil fuels]]
Article 56 of the [[Constitution of Turkey|Turkish Constitution]] states:
<blockquote>Everyone has the right to live in a healthy and balanced environment. It is the duty of the State and citizens to improve the natural environment, to protect the environmental health and to prevent environmental pollution.<ref>{{cite web |title=Constitution of Turkey |url=https://global.tbmm.gov.tr/docs/constitution_en.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200209123304/https://global.tbmm.gov.tr/docs/constitution_en.pdf |archive-date=9 February 2020 |access-date=20 September 2020 |website=[[Grand National Assembly of Turkey]]}}</ref></blockquote>

A similar clause in the constitution of the US state of [[Montana]] has been used to declare laws that support fossil fuels unconstitutional.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Noor |first1=Dharna |date=14 August 2023 |title='Gamechanger': judge rules in favor of young activists in US climate trial {{!}} Montana {{!}} The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2023/aug/14/montana-climate-trial-young-activists-judge-order |access-date=2023-08-16 |website=amp.theguardian.com}}</ref>

=== 2000s ===
The [[Justice and Development Party (Turkey)|Justice and Development Party (AK Party)]], led by [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]], was elected to government in 2003 and has been in power almost continuously since then. Turkey ratified the UNFCCC in 2004, but said it was unfair that it was included amongst the [[United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change#Annex I countries|Annex&nbsp;I (developed) countries]].<ref name=":27">{{cite web |last= |first= |date=17 June 2021 |title=Turkish environment minister dubs climate change a 'pandemic' |url=https://www.yenisafak.com/en/news/turkish-environment-minister-dubs-climate-change-a-pandemic-3574644 |access-date=27 June 2021 |website=[[Yeni Şafak]] |language=tr-TR}}</ref> When the treaty was signed in 1992 Turkey had much lower emissions per person, and no historical responsibility for greenhouse gas emissions. So, the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Turkey)|Foreign Ministry]] argue that Turkey should have been grouped with non-Annex developing countries, which can receive climate finance from the Green Climate Fund.<ref name=":17">{{cite web |title=United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Kyoto Protocol |url=http://www.mfa.gov.tr/united-nations-framework-convention-on-climate-change-_unfccc_-and-the-kyoto-protocol.en.mfa |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200719211828/http://www.mfa.gov.tr/united-nations-framework-convention-on-climate-change-_unfccc_-and-the-kyoto-protocol.en.mfa |archive-date=19 July 2020 |access-date=18 March 2021 |website=[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Turkey)|Republic of Turkey Ministry of Foreign Affairs]]}}</ref> Turkey ratified the [[Kyoto Protocol]] in 2009.<ref name=":16">{{cite web |title=Turkey |url=https://unfccc.int/node/61221 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191125190449/http://unfccc.int/node/61221 |archive-date=25 November 2019 |access-date=18 March 2021 |website=[[UNFCCC]]}}</ref>

=== 2010s ===
In a 2011 dispute over air pollution in Turkey, the main opposition [[Republican People's Party]] criticised the government for prioritising fossil fuels.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Demirci |first1=Elif |last2=Top |first2=Turaç |title=CHP iklim değişikliği raporunu açıkladı |trans-title=Republican People's Party explains climate change report |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/gundem/chp-iklim-degisikligi-raporunu-acikladi-17984108 |access-date=18 March 2021 |newspaper=[[Hürriyet]] |language=tr}}</ref> The Climate Change and Air Management Coordination Board ({{langx|tr|İklim Değişikliği ve Hava Yönetimi Koordinasyon Kurulu}}) was a government agency of the [[Republic of Turkey]], responsible for coordinating policy against [[air pollution in Turkey]] and climate change in Turkey; board meetings were chaired by the [[Ministry of Environment and Urban Planning (Turkey)|Minister of Environment and Urban Planning]].<ref>{{cite web |title=İkli̇m Deği̇şi̇kli̇ği̇ Ve Hava Yöneti̇mi̇ Koordi̇nasyon Kurulu Çalişma Usul Ve Esaslari Hakkinda Yönerge |url=https://webdosya.csb.gov.tr/db/iklim/webmenu/webmenu12631.pdf |accessdate=22 April 2019 |publisher=[[Ministry of Environment and Urban Planning (Turkey)]]}}</ref> The Climate Change and Air Management Coordination Board was created to coordinate government departments, and included three business organisations.<ref>{{cite web |title=Teşkilat Yapısı |trans-title=Organizational Structure |url=https://iklim.csb.gov.tr/teskilat-yapisi-i-4368 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190422073732/https://iklim.csb.gov.tr/teskilat-yapisi-i-4368 |archive-date=22 April 2019 |access-date=30 April 2019 |publisher=[[Ministry of Environment and Urban Planning (Turkey)]] |language=tr}}</ref> The Environment Ministry chaired it, though other ministries have considerable influence over climate change policy. The Energy Ministry has an Environment and Climate Department (responsible for the GHG inventory) and the [[Ministry of Treasury and Finance (Turkey)|Ministry of Treasury and Finance]] leads on climate financing.<ref name=":10" />{{Rp|40}}{{Obsolete source|date=October 2026}} Despite the [[Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources (Turkey)|Energy Ministry]] being represented on the board, in 2018 the [[European Commission]] criticised the lack of co-ordination between the climate change policy and [[energy policy of Turkey]].<ref>[https://ec.europa.eu/neighbourhood-enlargement/sites/near/files/20180417-turkey-report.pdf Turkey 2018 Report p92], European Commission, 17 April 2018</ref> Energy policy included mining more coal<ref name="MinEn">{{cite web |title=Coal |url=http://www.enerji.gov.tr/en-US/Pages/Coal |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180917110843/http://www.enerji.gov.tr/en-US/Pages/Coal |archive-date=17 September 2018 |accessdate=22 April 2019 |publisher=[[Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources (Turkey)]]}}</ref> and subsidizing coal-fired power stations.<ref>{{cite news |date=1 April 2019 |title=TEAİŞ, 2019 Yılı Şubat Ayı Kapasite Mekanizması Ödeme Listesini Açıkladı |url=https://www.enerjiportali.com/teais-2019-yili-subat-ayi-kapasite-mekanizmasi-odeme-listesini-acikladi/ |publisher=Enerji Portalı}}</ref> The board's decisions were not binding.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 December 2021 |title=Turkey ramps up efforts to reach 2053 climate goal - Turkey News |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkey-ramps-up-efforts-to-reach-2053-climate-goal-170182 |access-date=2022-01-04 |website=Hürriyet Daily News |language=en}}</ref> 

In 2018 a report outlining [[carbon market]] policy options for Turkey was submitted to the board.<ref>{{cite web |title=Turkey |url=https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/?option=com_etsmap&task=export&format=pdf&layout=list&systems[]=66 |accessdate=22 April 2019 |publisher=International Carbon Action Partnership}}</ref>

Turkey signed the Paris Agreement in 2016 but did not ratify it.<ref name=":16" /> In 2015 Turkey declared its intention to achieve "up to a 21% reduction in GHG emissions from the Business as Usual level by 2030".<ref name=":17" /> But because "Business as Usual" was assumed to be such a large increase, the "21% reduction" would have been an increase of over 7% per year<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 August 2021 |title=How climate targets compare against a common baseline |url=https://www.economist.com/graphic-detail/2021/08/07/how-climate-targets-compare-against-a-common-baseline |access-date=16 September 2021 |newspaper=The Economist |issn=0013-0613}}</ref> to around double the 2020 level.<ref name=":34">{{cite web |last1=Climate Action Tracker |first1=Turkey |title=Turkey |url=https://climateactiontracker.org/countries/turkey/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180614203500/https://climateactiontracker.org/countries/turkey/ |archive-date=14 June 2018 |access-date=30 November 2020 |website=[[Climate Action Tracker]] |publisher=Climate Action Tracker}}</ref>

In 2019, Ümit Şahin, who teaches climate change at [[Sabancı University]], said that Turkey saw industrialised Western countries as solely responsible.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last1=Şahin |first1=Ümit |last2=Türkkan |first2=Seçil |date=January 2019 |title=Turkey's Climate Policies Have Reached a Deadlock: It Takes Courage to Resolve It |url=https://www.hyd.org.tr/attachments/article/511/saha2en.pdf |magazine=saha |pages=24–30 |volume=Special Issue 2 |issn=2149-7885 |quote=According to him, Turkey's problem is not that it doesn't take climate change seriously, but that it downplays its share in creating the problem and sees industrialized Western countries as solely responsible}}</ref>{{Rp|24}} While discussing their limited actions on climate change, Turkey and other countries cited the forthcoming [[United States withdrawal from the Paris Agreement]].<ref>{{cite news |last=McGrath |first=Matt |date=3 December 2018 |title=Climate change: 'Trump effect' threatens Paris pact |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-46384828 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190424174404/https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-46384828 |archive-date=24 April 2019 |access-date=24 April 2019 |work=[[BBC]]}}</ref> Turkey was the 16th largest [[List of countries by greenhouse gas emissions|emitting country]] in 2019.<ref name=":11">{{cite web |last=Yackley |first=Ayla Jean |date=27 October 2020 |title=With climate absent from Ankara's agenda, Turkey's Greens sense an opening |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/climate-change-ankara-agenda-turkey-greens-sense-opening/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201110202832/https://www.politico.eu/article/climate-change-ankara-agenda-turkey-greens-sense-opening/ |archive-date=10 November 2020 |access-date=18 November 2020 |website=[[Politico]]}}</ref>{{efn|Overtaken by [[Greenhouse gas emissions by Australia]]}}

During the 2019 UN Climate Action Summit on achieving [[carbon neutrality]] by 2050, Turkey co-led the coalition on the [[Low-carbon economy|decarbonization]] of land transport.<ref name="UN2019">{{cite web |title=Track #7: Infrastructure, Cities and Local Action |url=https://www.un.org/sustainabledevelopment/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/WP-Infrastructures-Cities-and-Local-Action.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210417023004/https://www.un.org/sustainabledevelopment/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/WP-Infrastructures-Cities-and-Local-Action.pdf |archive-date=17 April 2021 |access-date=13 September 2019 |website=[[United Nations Human Settlements Programme]]}}</ref> {{As of|2019}}, the government aimed to keep the share of coal in the energy portfolio at around the same level in the medium and long term. This was explained, in part, because of Turkey's desire to have a diverse mix of energy sources. Rather than increase imports of gas, it wanted to retain domestic coal, albeit with safeguards to reduce the impact on human health and the environment.<ref name=":25" />{{Rp|20}} İklim Haber (''Climate News'') and [[KONDA Research and Consultancy]] found in 2018 that [[public opinion on climate change]] prefers solar and wind power.<ref name="Website-5">{{cite web |year=2018 |title=Turkey Climate Survey |url=https://www.iklimhaber.org/climatesurvey2018/ |website=İklim Haber}}</ref>

=== 2020s ===

==== Local politics and a just transition ====
{{See also|Coal in Turkey#Employment}}
[[File:Karslı cocuklarin soma icn yaptiklati maket--Muhammetilbas-com 2014-05-29 23-32.JPG|thumb|Children's models commemorating the [[Soma mine disaster]] – "This is how they earn their daily bread"|alt=colourful tiny model trucks containing coal with "Soma" written on the side]]
[[File:Catalagzi Termik Santrali.jpg|thumb|alt=two tall chimneys and large buildings lit up at night|[[Çatalağzı power station]] in [[Zonguldak]]: Turkey's first coal mining region would need help to give up.]]
Each province will prepare a climate action plan to start in 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-17 |title=Türkiye designates two new marine national parks |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkiye-designates-two-new-marine-national-parks-225683 |access-date=2026-10-26 |website=Hürriyet Daily News |language=en}}</ref> Although the transition to clean energy increases employment in Turkey as a whole,<ref name=":36" /> for example in wind and solar power<ref name=":21" />{{Rp|6}} and energy efficiency of buildings,<ref name="Buildings Performance Institute Europe and SHURA Energy Transition Center1" /> lost jobs may be concentrated in certain locations and sectors.<ref name=":20" />{{Rp|48}} For example, closing [[Şırnak Silopi power station]] and the coal mines in [[Şırnak Province]] could increase already high unemployment there.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Elçi |first=Dicle Özcan Elçi |date=June 2018 |title=In without Social Security Conditions Şırnak Coal Mines Workers |url=https://app.trdizin.gov.tr/publication/paper/detail/TWpJek56UTNOdz09 |journal=Çalışma ve Toplum |issue=48 |pages=169–197}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Özcan |first=Dicle |date=2016 |title=Çalışma ve Toplum Dergisi |url=https://www.calismatoplum.org/makale/guvencesiz-calisma-kosullarindasirnak-komur-ocaklaricalisanlari |access-date=26 April 2021 |website=calismatoplum.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426062534/https://www.calismatoplum.org/makale/guvencesiz-calisma-kosullarindasirnak-komur-ocaklaricalisanlari |archive-date=26 April 2021 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Because carbon pricing would be somewhat [[Regressive tax|regressive]] economists say that poor people should be compensated.<ref>{{Cite report |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/resrep70418 |title=The Distributional Effects of Carbon Pricing in Türkiye |last1=Can |first1=Zeynep Gizem |last2=O’Donoghue |first2=Cathal |last3=Sologon |first3=Denisa |date=2025 |publisher=IZA - Institute of Labor Economics |jstor=resrep70418 }}</ref> In 2024 the government said it will make a national policy for a [[just transition]];<ref name=":55" />{{Rp|location=section 4.6}} policy to quit high-carbon, such as coal, is lacking.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gündüzyeli |first1=Elif |last2=Kutluay |first2=Duygu |date=7 February 2020 |title=Turkey's dilemma: risky coal or clean development |url=https://beyond-coal.eu/2020/02/07/turkeys-dilemma-risky-coal-or-clean-development/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200716132424/https://beyond-coal.eu/2020/02/07/turkeys-dilemma-risky-coal-or-clean-development/ |archive-date=16 July 2020 |access-date=16 July 2020 |website=Europe Beyond Coal}}</ref> Similarly, it is hard for livestock farmers to make a profit,<ref name=":3" /> so a sudden removal of subsidies would be an economic shock. But, unlike in neighbouring Greece,<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 September 2021 |title=Greece to establish company for transforming coal land property |url=https://balkangreenenergynews.com/greece-to-establish-company-for-transforming-coal-land-property/ |access-date=1 October 2021 |website=Balkan Green Energy News |language=en-US}}</ref> there have been no public debates about a just transition.<ref name="ClimT">{{Cite report |url=https://www.climate-transparency.org/countries/europe/turkey |title=Turkey, Country Profile |year=2020 |publisher=Climate Transparency}}</ref> 

According to former Economy Minister [[Kemal Derviş]], many people will benefit from the green transition, but the losses will be concentrated on specific groups, making them more visible and politically disruptive.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Derviş |first1=Kemal |last2=Strauss |first2=Sebastian |date=20 August 2019 |title=The real obstacle to climate action |url=https://www.brookings.edu/opinions/the-real-obstacle-to-climate-action/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030021722/https://www.brookings.edu/opinions/the-real-obstacle-to-climate-action/ |archive-date=30 October 2020 |access-date=11 October 2020 |website=[[Brookings Institution|Brookings]]}}</ref>{{anchor|Cities}}At the municipal level, [[Antalya]], [[Bornova]], [[Bursa]], [[Çankaya, Ankara (district)|Çankaya]], Eskişehir Tepebaşı, [[Gaziantep]], [[İzmir]], [[Kadıköy]], [[Maltepe, Istanbul|Maltepe]], [[Nilüfer, Bursa|Nilüfer]] and [[Seferihisar]] have [[sustainable energy]] and climate plans.<ref>{{cite web |title=Action plans |url=https://www.covenantofmayors.eu/plans-and-actions/action-plans.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200923092921/https://covenantofmayors.eu/plans-and-actions/action-plans.html |archive-date=23 September 2020 |access-date=2 September 2020 |website=[[Covenant of Mayors]]}}</ref> A 2021 academic study of local [[climate change politics]] said that "local climate action planning takes place independent from the national efforts yet with a commitment to international agreements" and that better co-ordination between local and national government would help planning for [[climate change adaptation]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Peker |first1=Ender |title=Governance of Climate Responsive Cities |last2=Ataöv |first2=Anlı |date=2021 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |isbn=978-3-030-73399-5 |editor-last=Peker |editor-first=Ender |series=The Urban Book Series |location=Cham |pages=21–42 |language=en |chapter=Barriers to Implementing Local Climate Action Plans in Turkey: Searching for a Potential Way Out |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-73399-5_3 |editor2-last=Ataöv |editor2-first=Anlı |s2cid=239744399}}</ref> Turkey ratified the Paris Agreement in 2021: according to [[Politico]] the country was persuaded by a 3.2 billion dollar loan from France and Germany for its [[energy transition]], and Turkey's chief negotiator said the threat of the EU CBAM was a factor.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-11-06 |title=EU's looming carbon tax nudged Turkey toward Paris climate accord, envoy says |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism-turkey-paris-accord-climate-change/ |access-date=2022-04-13 |website=POLITICO |language=en-US}}</ref>

==== National Politics ====
Turkish citizens took [[individual and political action on climate change]] to the streets<ref>{{cite web |last=Neumann |first=Laura |date=21 September 2019 |title=Activists in Turkey demonstrate with call to 'unite behind the science' on climate change |url=http://www.middleeasteye.net/news/activists-turkey-demonstrate-call-unite-behind-science-climate-change |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190924013655/https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/activists-turkey-demonstrate-call-unite-behind-science-climate-change |archive-date=24 September 2019 |access-date=24 January 2020 |website=[[Middle East Eye]]}}</ref> and online,<ref>{{cite web |last=Tekin |first=Aynur |date=3 April 2020 |title=Turkey's first digital strike is for the climate |url=https://www.duvarenglish.com/environment/2020/04/03/turkeys-first-digital-strike-is-for-the-climate/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200423091230/https://www.duvarenglish.com/environment/2020/04/03/turkeys-first-digital-strike-is-for-the-climate/ |archive-date=23 April 2020 |access-date=5 May 2020 |website=[[Gazete Duvar]]}}</ref> including children demanding action<ref>{{cite web |date=12 August 2019 |title=Turkey's 11-year-old activist demands grown-up action on climate change |url=https://ahvalnews.com/climate-crisis/turkeys-11-year-old-activist-demands-grown-action-climate-change |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190904141307/https://ahvalnews.com/climate-crisis/turkeys-11-year-old-activist-demands-grown-action-climate-change |archive-date=4 September 2019 |access-date=4 September 2019 |website=[[Ahval]]}}</ref> and petitioning the UN.<ref>{{cite web |last=Teirstein |first=Zoya |date=25 September 2019 |title=What the climate petition filed by 16 kids at the U.N. really means |url=https://grist.org/article/what-the-climate-petition-filed-by-16-kids-at-the-u-n-really-means/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190927123516/https://grist.org/article/what-the-climate-petition-filed-by-16-kids-at-the-u-n-really-means/ |archive-date=27 September 2019 |access-date=27 September 2019 |website=[[Grist (magazine)|Grist]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=23 September 2019 |title=Communication to the Committee on the Rights of the Child |url=https://childrenvsclimatecrisis.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/2019.09.23-CRC-communication-Sacchi-et-al-v.-Argentina-et-al-2.pdf |website=[[Earthjustice]]}}</ref>{{Rp|29}}  [[Green Party (Turkey)|Turkey's Green Party]] called for an end to coal burning<ref name=":11" /> and the phasing out of all fossil-fuel use by 2050.<ref>{{cite web |date=21 September 2020 |title=Greens in Turkey Launch Green Party! |url=https://yesiller.org.tr/2020/09/21/greens-in-turkey-launch-green-party/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201001232556/https://yesiller.org.tr/2020/09/21/greens-in-turkey-launch-green-party/ |archive-date=1 October 2020 |access-date=22 September 2020 |website=[[Green Party (Turkey)]]}}</ref> 

After the 2020/21 droughts, the [[Nationalist Movement Party]] (the smaller party in the governing coalition) said that climate change is a national security issue.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bakırmekik |first=Melis |date=26 February 2021 |title=MHP'li Kalyoncu: İklim değişikliği uluslararası terörden daha tehlikeli |trans-title=MHP's Kalyoncu: Climate change is more dangerous than international terrorism |url=https://www.egetv.com.tr/mhpli-kalyoncu-iklim-degisikligi-uluslararasi-terorden-daha-tehlikeli-41146 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210227125422/https://www.egetv.com.tr/mhpli-kalyoncu-iklim-degisikligi-uluslararasi-terorden-daha-tehlikeli-41146 |archive-date=27 February 2021 |access-date=18 March 2021 |website=Ege TV |language=tr}}</ref> The threat of climate change had already been [[Securitization (international relations)#As a tactic|securitized]] by Environment Minister Murat Kurum back in 2019.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bir |first=Burak |date=11 December 2019 |title=Climate change is national security issue: Turkey |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/environment/climate-change-is-national-security-issue-turkey/1670673 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191212173349/https://www.aa.com.tr/en/environment/climate-change-is-national-security-issue-turkey/1670673 |archive-date=12 December 2019 |access-date=22 March 2021 |website=www.aa.com.tr |publisher=[[Anadolu Agency]]}}</ref> Also following on from the droughts,  a Parliamentary Research Commission wrote a report.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TBMM Kütüphanesi Açık Erişim Sistemi |url=https://acikerisim.tbmm.gov.tr/items/103ace3d-1225-40a1-b290-b9e4815b2067 |access-date=2026-10-01 |website=acikerisim.tbmm.gov.tr}}</ref> 

The national energy plan published in 2022 expected 1.7&nbsp;GW more coal power to be built,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://enerji.gov.tr/Media/Dizin/EIGM/tr/Raporlar/TUEP/T%C3%BCrkiye_National_Energy_Plan.pdf|title=TÜRKİYE NATIONAL ENERGY PLAN}}</ref> but the opposition CHP had already said that no more fossil fuel power plants should be built and that there should be carbon trading.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 October 2021 |title=CHP: Hızla harekete geçilmesi gerekiyor |url=https://www.milliyet.com.tr/siyaset/chp-hizla-harekete-gecilmesi-gerekiyor-6618149 |access-date=2021-10-13 |website=Milliyet |language=tr}}</ref> Businesses say the country needs to decarbonise so that money which would otherwise be lost to the CBAM remains in the country: NGOs and academics have such plans, however a February 2022 government-led "Climate Council" of all those groups and others issued over 200 recommendations,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Final Declaration |url=https://iklimsurasi.gov.tr/en/sayfa/final-declaration |access-date=2022-11-16 |website=iklimsurasi.gov.tr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231120051248/https://iklimsurasi.gov.tr/en/sayfa/final-declaration |archive-date=20 November 2023 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=KOMİSYON TAVSİYE KARARLARI |url=https://iklimsurasi.gov.tr/public/images/sonucbildirgesi.pdf |access-date=22 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230205143937/https://iklimsurasi.gov.tr/public/images/sonucbildirgesi.pdf |archive-date=5 February 2023 |url-status=dead}}</ref> but not one for coal phase out.<ref name=":47" /> European Climate Action Network Turkey complained that civil society is not properly represented in decision making and in particular that there were no organizations such as theirs in the " Emission Reduction Commission" of the Climate Council.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-04 |title=COP27 İklim Zirvesi: Türkiye 2053'te net sıfır emisyon hedefine ulaşmak için neler yapmalı? |url=https://www.bbc.com/turkce/articles/c9982p102qdo |access-date=2022-11-16 |website=BBC News Türkçe |language=tr}}</ref>

[[File:Renewable_energy_reduces_health_costs_in_Turkey.jpg|thumb|Renewable energy reduces health costs in Turkey]]
{{As of|2019}} the [[Ministry of Health (Turkey)|Health Ministry]] is not actively involved in the permitting of industrial facilities, such as [[coal-fired power station]]s, which cause deaths due to air pollution.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://www.temizhavahakki.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/Hava-Kirlili%C4%9Fi-ve-Sa%C4%9Fl%C4%B1k-Etkileri-Kara-Rapor-2019.pdf |title=Hava Kirliliği ve Sağlık Etkileri KARA RAPOR |date=11 May 2019 |pages=56 |access-date=11 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190606182418/https://www.temizhavahakki.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/Hava-Kirlili%C4%9Fi-ve-Sa%C4%9Fl%C4%B1k-Etkileri-Kara-Rapor-2019.pdf |archive-date=6 June 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Although the Health and Agriculture Ministries coordinate with each other, there is no formal agreement between Health and Energy or Transport as of 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Health and climate change: country profile 2022: Turkey - Turkey {{!}} ReliefWeb |url=https://reliefweb.int/report/turkey/health-and-climate-change-country-profile-2022-turkey |access-date=2022-06-04 |website=reliefweb.int |language=en}}</ref>

The board was replaced with the Climate Change and Adaptation Coordination Board (CCAMC) for a short time, and a Climate Change Presidency was created,<ref>{{Cite web |last=iklim.gov.tr |title=İDUKK Kurul Hakkında - İklim Değişikliği Başkanlığı |url=https://www.iklim.gov.tr/idukk-i-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809090007/https://www.iklim.gov.tr/idukk-i-13 |archive-date=2025-08-09 |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=iklim.gov.tr |language=tr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=iklim.gov.tr |title=Coordination Commity of Climate Change Adaptation - About Commity - İklim Değişikliği Başkanlığı |url=https://iklim.gov.tr/en/coordination-commity-of-climate-change-adaptation-i-76 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114100309/https://iklim.gov.tr/en/coordination-commity-of-climate-change-adaptation-i-76 |archive-date=2025-01-14 |access-date=2026-01-17 |website=iklim.gov.tr |language=en}}</ref> (also translated as “Directorate of Climate Change”).<ref>{{Cite web |last=iklim.gov.tr |title=About Us - İklim Değişikliği Başkanlığı |url=https://www.iklim.gov.tr/en/about-us-i-75 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250911185452/https://www.iklim.gov.tr/en/about-us-i-75 |archive-date=2025-09-11 |access-date=2026-01-17 |website=iklim.gov.tr |language=en}}</ref>

==== International politics ====
Turkey and some other member countries say the [[Energy Charter Treaty]] should be changed to help with decarbonization, but because changes must be unanimous this is unlikely to happen.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Energy Charter Treaty: A Real Threat to Climate Action Plans |url=http://turkishpolicy.com/blog/55/the-energy-charter-treaty-a-real-threat-to-climate-action-plans |access-date=1 October 2021 |website=Turkish Policy Quarterly |language=en}}</ref> [[TPAO|Turkish Petroleum Corporation]] (TPAO) is in discussions with private-sector companies about investment in Black Sea fossil gas.<ref name=":13a">{{cite web |last=Ersoy |first=Ercan |date=8 February 2021 |title=Turkish Petroleum mulls partnerships for multi-billion Black Sea gas project |url=https://www.worldoil.com/news/2021/2/8/turkish-petroleum-mulls-partnerships-for-multi-billion-black-sea-gas-project |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209114304/https://www.worldoil.com/news/2021/2/8/turkish-petroleum-mulls-partnerships-for-multi-billion-black-sea-gas-project |archive-date=9 February 2021 |access-date=16 March 2021 |website=worldoil.com}}</ref> China funded [[Emba Hunutlu power station|Emba Hunutlu coal-fired power station]] started up in 2022.

The government says that, as a developing country having less than 1% responsibility for historical greenhouse gas emissions, Turkey's position under the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement is not fair at all.<ref>{{cite web |date=22 November 2020 |title=Statement of the Spokesperson of Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mr. Hami Aksoy, in Response to a Question Regarding Turkey's Putting on the Record its Determination to Obtain a Fair Position Under the International Climate Change Regime in the G20 Leaders' Declaration |url=http://www.mfa.gov.tr/sc_-114_-turkiye-nin-uluslararasi-iklim-degisikligiyle-mucadele-rejimi-hk-sc.en.mfa |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210128024659/http://www.mfa.gov.tr/sc_-114_-turkiye-nin-uluslararasi-iklim-degisikligiyle-mucadele-rejimi-hk-sc.en.mfa |archive-date=28 January 2021 |access-date=13 December 2020 |website=[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Turkey)]]}}</ref> However some academics say that low historical greenhouse gas emissions can only be used as a fairness justification under [[International Environmental Law|international environmental law]] by [[least developed countries]] and [[Small Island Developing States|small island developing states]].<ref name=":35">{{Cite web |last=Nicolas.Fux |date=9 September 2021 |title=National 'fair shares' in reducing greenhouse gas emissions within the principled framework of international environmental law |url=https://newclimate.org/2021/09/09/national-fair-shares-in-reducing-greenhouse-gas-emissions-within-framework-of-international-env-law/ |access-date=12 September 2021 |website=NewClimate Institute |language=en-GB}}</ref> They say that almost all G20 countries, including Turkey, should reduce their emissions below the 2010 level.<ref name=":35" /> Nevertheless, the same academics say that countries with higher historical emissions should reduce emissions more.<ref name=":35" />

[[Environmental lawyers]] became more active in the 2020s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Europe in transition |url=https://caneurope.org/work-areas/europe-in-transition/ |access-date=25 April 2021 |website=[[Climate Action Network]] Europe |language=en-GB |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210425062637/https://caneurope.org/work-areas/europe-in-transition/ |archive-date=25 April 2021 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The Paris Agreement was ratified by parliament shortly before the [[2021 United Nations Climate Change Conference]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 September 2021 |title=Turkey set to submit Paris climate pact to parliament next month: President – Turkey News |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkey-set-to-submit-paris-climate-pact-to-parliament-next-month-president-168049 |access-date=22 September 2021 |website=Hürriyet Daily News |language=en}}</ref>

Hakan Mining and Generation Industry & Trade Inc. constructed [[Gisagara Thermal Power Station|Gisagara peat-fired power station]] in Rwanda, which was delayed by [[Climate change in Rwanda|climate change]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nkurunziza |first=Michel |date=2022-05-24 |title=How peat power projects were derailed by climate change, Covid-19 |url=https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/196069/News/how-peat-power-projects-were-derailed-by-climate-change-covid-19 |access-date=2026-09-30 |website=The New Times |language=en}}</ref> but started supplying the grid in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nkurunziza |first=Michel |date=2026-08-09 |title=How Gisagara peat power plant could double production to 70MW |url=https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/38036/news/energy/how-gisagara-peat-power-plant-could-double-production-to-70mw |access-date=2026-09-30 |website=The New Times |language=en}}</ref>

Academics doubt that emissions could be reduced from a 2038 peak to zero by 2053,<ref name=":50">{{Cite web |date=2022-11-16 |title=COP 27: Türkiye'nin yeni iklim hedefini uzmanlar nasıl yorumluyor? |url=https://www.bbc.com/turkce/articles/ceq20288wglo |access-date=2022-11-16 |website=BBC News Türkçe |language=tr}}</ref> and say that delaying Turkey's energy transition is more expensive than starting it at once.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Decarbonization Pathway for Turkey: Sectoral Cost-Benefit Analysis (2020-2030) |url=https://ipc.sabanciuniv.edu/en/publications |access-date=2022-11-16 |website=ipc.sabanciuniv.edu |language=en}}</ref> The 2053 target was reportedly set without consulting the Energy Ministry, and as of 2023 that ministry has not published a decarbonization roadmap.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Ergenç |first1=Ceren |last2=Göçer |first2=Derya |date=5 May 2023 |title=China's Response to Türkiye's Volatile Authoritarianism |url=https://carnegieendowment.org/research/2023/05/chinas-response-to-turkiyes-volatile-authoritarianism?lang=en |website=[[Carnegie Endowment for International Peace]]}}</ref> Turkey will host the [[2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=COP31 |title=COP31 Türkiye Antalya 2026 UN Climate Change Conference |url=https://cop31.tr/ |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=COP31 Türkiye |language=en}}</ref>

==Adaptation==
The [[Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change]] coordinates activities to combat climate change in Turkey.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Turkey — Climate-ADAPT |url=https://climate-adapt.eea.europa.eu/countries-regions/countries/turkey |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220812034220/https://climate-adapt.eea.europa.eu/countries-regions/countries/turkey/ |archive-date=12 August 2022 |access-date=2020-12-01 |website=climate-adapt.eea.europa.eu}}</ref>  The Twelfth Development Plan (2024–2028) mentions adaptation.<ref>{{Cite report |url=https://www.sbb.gov.tr/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Twelfth-Development-Plan_2024-2028.pdf |title=Twelfth Development Plan (2024-2028) |date=31 October 2023 |publisher=[[President of Turkey]] |access-date=16 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240913043453/https://www.sbb.gov.tr/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Twelfth-Development-Plan_2024-2028.pdf |archive-date=13 September 2024 |url-status=dead}}</ref>{{Rp|pages=|page=218}} A national strategy and action plan for 2024 to 2030 adaptation to climate change has been published,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Climate Change Adaptation Strategy and Action Plan (2024-2030) |url=https://iklim.gov.tr/db/english/icerikler/files/Uyum(1).pdf}}</ref> but {{As of|2026|lc=y}} Turkey has yet to submit a National Adaptation Plan to the [[UNFCCC]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Submitted NAPs from developing country Parties {{!}} NAP Central |url=https://napcentral.org/submitted-naps |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=napcentral.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NAPs shared by developed country Parties {{!}} NAP Central |url=https://napcentral.org/developedcountriesnaps |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=napcentral.org}}</ref>

Agriculture Minister [[Bekir Pakdemirli]] said in 2023 that irrigation was being modernized and that thirsty crops, such as corn, were being swapped out of [[agriculture in Turkey]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Turkey to modernize irrigation system, farming to save water |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/energy/energy-security/turkey-to-modernize-irrigation-system-farming-to-save-water/33597 |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=www.aa.com.tr}}</ref> [[Xeriscaping|Water-conserving landscaping]] of green spaces in cities has been suggested,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Çetin|first1=Nefise|last2=Mansuroğlu|first2=Sibel|last3=Kalaycı Önaç|first3=Ayşe|year=2018|title=Xeriscaping Feasibility as an Urban Adaptation Method for Global Warming: A Case Study from Turkey|journal=Pol. J. Environ. Stud.|volume=27|issue=3|pages=1009–1018|doi=10.15244/pjoes/76678|doi-access=free|bibcode=2018PJES...27.1009C }}</ref> and Istanbul has a climate change action plan.<ref>{{cite web|title=İstanbul İklim Değişikliği Eylem Planı|trans-title=Istanbul climate change action plan|url=https://www.iklim.istanbul/|url-status=live|access-date=17 April 2019|language=tr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180830231849/https://www.iklim.istanbul/ |archive-date=2018-08-30 }}</ref> A 2023 study suggested that local climate change plans should be better integrated with local [[Spatial planning|spatial plans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Local Coping with Climate Change: Integrating Climate Action Plans and Spatial Plans |url=https://planningdesign-ataunipress.org/Content/files/sayilar/2/PLANARCH_202322039_nlm_new_indd.pdf |language=tr |access-date=1 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240101105032/https://planningdesign-ataunipress.org/Content/files/sayilar/2/PLANARCH_202322039_nlm_new_indd.pdf |archive-date=1 January 2024 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The [[World Bank Group|World Bank]] is funding [[flood control]] infrastructure.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-24 |title=Flood control facilities to be built with World Bank funding - Türkiye News |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/flood-control-facilities-to-be-built-with-world-bank-funding-213951 |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=Hürriyet Daily News |language=en}}</ref>

== Society and culture ==

=== Education, research and access to information ===
[[Climate change education]] is an option in 6th, 7th and 8th grades of [[education in Turkey]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |title="ENVIRONMENT EDUCATION AND CLIMATE CHANGE" CURRICULUM IS COMPLETED |url=https://www.meb.gov.tr/environment-education-and-climate-change-curriculum-is-completed/haber/25946/en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220718215457/http://www.meb.gov.tr/environment-education-and-climate-change-curriculum-is-completed/haber/25946/en |archive-date=18 July 2022 |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=www.meb.gov.tr |language= |url-status=live }}</ref> As of 2025 there is not much teacher training or school materials, however there is higher education and research at [[Boğaziçi University]]'s Center for Climate Change and Policy Studies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Türkiye {{!}} Climate change communication and education {{!}} Education Profiles |url=https://education-profiles.org/northern-africa-and-western-asia/turkiye/~climate-change-communication-and-education |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=education-profiles.org}}</ref> In 2025 results will be measured by the [[Programme for International Student Assessment]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stock |first=Petra |date=2024-12-23 |title=How to teach climate change so 15-year-olds can act |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2024/dec/24/how-to-teach-climate-change-so-15-year-olds-can-act |access-date=2025-01-23 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> İklim Masası  (Climate Desk) is a news platform with experts writing for the public and as a reference for journalists.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Climate crisis is changing Turkey's fire regime |url=https://bianet.org/haber/climate-crisis-is-changing-turkey-s-fire-regime-310069 |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=bianet.org |language=en}}</ref>

Sabancı University's Shura Energy Transition Center is researching [[decarbonization pathways]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Decarbonization Pathways for Turkey 2020–2050 – Modelling Study Terms of Reference |url=https://ipc.sabanciuniv.edu/Content/Images/CKeditorImages/20200709-23075797.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210417023009/https://ipc.sabanciuniv.edu/Content/Images/CKeditorImages/20200709-23075797.pdf |archive-date=17 April 2021 |access-date=26 November 2020 |publisher=[[Sabancı University]]}}</ref> [[Linear regression]], expert judgement and local integrated assessment modelling is used for non-energy projections.<ref name=":24" />{{Rp|8}}<ref name="rep4" />{{Rp|33}} Emissions from industry have been [[Energy modeling|modelled]] by the Energy Ministry and the [[Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey]] using [[MARKAL|TIMES]]-MACRO.<ref name="rep4" />{{Rp|33}} A "Climate Change Platform" is planned to share studies and data.<ref name=":10" />{{Rp|46}}<span class="anchor" id="Perspectives on emissions"></span>Although the OECD praised the government's [[monitoring, reporting and verification]] (MRV) system and said in 2021 that it covers half of total emissions,<ref name="OECD2021" />{{Rp|61}} unlike the public sharing of data in the [[European Union Emissions Trading System|EU emission trading system]], much detailed emissions data in Turkey is not public.<ref>{{cite web |title=EU Emission Trading System Directive Preliminary Regulatory Impact Assessment (Pre-RIA) |url=http://www.lowcarbonturkey.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Annex-3_ETS-RIA-eng.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190430095304/http://www.lowcarbonturkey.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Annex-3_ETS-RIA-eng.pdf |archive-date=30 April 2019 |access-date=30 April 2019 |page=26}}</ref> However in 2025 Hayrettin Kurt, Chairman of the Audit Committee at the [[World Energy Council]] Turkish National Committee, said that facility level data from the [[Turkish Emissions Trading System]] will be disclosed to the public.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kurt |first=Hayrettin |date=2025-09-30 |title=Restoring the Lost Balance on Land and Sea: Turkey's Climate Law |url=https://politicstoday.org/restoring-the-lost-balance-on-land-and-sea-turkeys-climate-law/ |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=Politics Today |language=en-US}}</ref> Quantitative estimates of the impact of individual government policies on emissions have not been made or are not publicly available;<ref name=":25" />{{Rp|20}} neither are projections of long-term policy impacts.<ref name=":25" />{{Rp|21}} An expert review of Turkey's GHG report published in 2023 noted that over 50 recommendations made in previous expert reviews had not yet been addressed.<ref>{{Cite tech report |url=https://unfccc.int/documents/637654 |title=Report on the individual review of the inventory submission of Türkiye submitted in 2023. Note by the expert review team |date=2024-04-02 |id=FCCC/ARR/2023/TUR |work=[[UNFCCC]]}}</ref> Space-based measurements of the signs of emissions has allowed public monitoring of the [[megacity]] of Istanbul and high emitting power plants since the early-2020s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Pan |first1=Guanna |last2=Xu |first2=Yuan |last3=Ma |first3=Jieqi |date=1 January 2021 |title=The potential of CO<sub>2</sub> satellite monitoring for climate governance: A review |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301479720313487 |url-status=live |journal=Journal of Environmental Management |volume=277 |doi=10.1016/j.jenvman.2020.111423 |issn=0301-4797 |pmid=33031999 |s2cid=222237434 |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201103080312/https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301479720313487 |archive-date=3 November 2020 |access-date=18 November 2020 |article-number=111423}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Couture |first=Heather D. |date=11 August 2020 |title=How to Track the Emissions of Every Power Plant on the Planet from Space |url=https://spectrum.ieee.org/how-to-track-the-emissions-of-every-power-plant-on-the-planet-from-space |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201130153347/https://spectrum.ieee.org/energywise/energy/fossil-fuels/how-to-track-the-emissions-of-every-power-plant-on-the-planet-from-space |archive-date=30 November 2020 |access-date=18 November 2020 |website=IEEE Spectrum: Technology, Engineering, and Science News}}</ref>

=== Activism ===
[[File:Küresel Isınmaya Hayır Mitingi, Kadıköy, İstanbul (08-12-2007).jpg|thumb|A 2007 climate change protest in [[Istanbul]].]]

Climate Network Türkiye is a coalition of [[Civil society organization|civil society organisations]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-05 |title=About - İklim Ağı |url=https://iklimagi.org/en/about/ |access-date=2026-09-02 |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[Islamic environmentalism|Muslim environmentalists]] and academics quote the [[Quran]] in support of their environmentalism.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bodetti|first=Austin|title=Why Turkish academic Ibrahim Ozdemir is pushing for an Islamic approach to environmentalism|url=https://www.alaraby.co.uk/english/indepth/2019/9/12/ibrahim-ozdemir-one-of-turkeys-most-prominent-environmentalists|access-date=2019-10-01|website=alaraby|date=12 September 2019 }}</ref> In [[Istanbul]] in 2015, [[Islamic]] leaders urged the world's 1.6 billion Muslims to help defeat climate change.<ref>[https://unfccc.int/news/islamic-declaration-on-climate-change "Islamic Declaration on Climate Change"] UNFCCC, 18 August 2015</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Islamic Declaration on Global Climate Change|url=http://www.ifees.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/10/climate_declarationmMWB.pdf|access-date=7 May 2019|publisher=The Islamic Foundation For Ecology And Environmental Sciences|archive-date=9 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200209110721/http://www.ifees.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/10/climate_declarationmMWB.pdf}}</ref>

In 2026 [[First Ladies of Turkey|first lady]] [[Emine Erdoğan]] called for reducing excessive consumption and waste.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-22 |title=Turkish first lady holds talks in New York - Türkiye News |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-first-lady-holds-talks-in-new-york-227191 |access-date=2026-10-10 |website=Hürriyet Daily News |language=en}}</ref> In 2019 some Turkish schoolchildren joined the [[School Strike for Climate]].<ref>{{Cite news|title='When adults fail, we need to take action,' says activist|website=[[Hürriyet Daily News]]|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/when-adults-fail-we-need-to-take-action-says-activist-146593|access-date=2019-10-01}}</ref>

====Media and arts====
[[File:Müze Gazhane in January 2024 05.jpg|thumb|[[Hasanpaşa Gasworks|Müze Gazhane]] in [[Kadıköy]] is the first climate change museum in Turkey.]]
In the 1990s independent ''[[Açık Radyo]]'' (Open Radio) broadcast some of the first [[media coverage of climate change]], and its founder [[:tr:Ömer Madra|Ömer Madra]] {{in lang|tr}} emphasises "The three Y's in the fight on climate change: ''Yerel'' (local) ''Yatay'' (horizontal) and ''Yavaş'' (slow, no resort to violence)."<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/local-activism-at-the-heart-of-fight-against-global-heating-151893|title=Local activism at the heart of fight against 'global heating'|website=[[Hürriyet Daily News]]|access-date=2020-02-10}}</ref> The station continues,<ref name=":14" /> and ''İklim Haber'' (Climate News) also covers climate change issues in Turkish and English.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hakkımızda|trans-title=About Us|url=https://www.iklimhaber.org/hakkimizda/|access-date=2020-11-25|website=İklim Haber|date=14 October 2017 |language=tr}}</ref> The climate impact of [[Coal power in Turkey|coal power]] is rarely discussed,<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |title=How journalists in Turkey are covering the climate crisis |url=https://ijnet.org/en/story/how-journalists-turkey-are-covering-climate-crisis |access-date=2023-12-15 |website=International Journalists' Network |language=en}}</ref> and nearly all [[Mass media in Turkey|Turkish media]] owners have financial interests in fossil fuels.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last1=Cengiz|first1=Pelin|last2=Zırığ|first2=Utku|last3=Şimşek|first3=Soner|date=January 2019|title=Thematic Journalism in Turkey: Environmental-Ecological Reporting|url=https://www.hyd.org.tr/attachments/article/511/saha2en.pdf|magazine=saha|volume=Special Issue 2|pages=16–23|issn=2149-7885}}</ref>{{Rp|17,20}} The media covers climate change only during extreme weather events, with insufficient expert opinions or civil-society perspectives.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last1=Şahin|first1=Ümit|last2=Türkkan|first2=Seçil|date=January 2019|title=Turkey's Climate Policies Have Reached a Deadlock: It Takes Courage to Resolve It|url=https://www.hyd.org.tr/attachments/article/511/saha2en.pdf|magazine=saha|volume=Special Issue 2|pages=24–30|issn=2149-7885}}</ref>{{Rp|28}} Some [[think tank]]s, such as [[Ember (non-profit organisation)|Ember]], are respected by both [[Industry in Turkey|industry]] and environmentalists.<ref name=":14" />  Ufuk Alparslan, Ember's regional lead, says that readers are enthused by [[Solar power in Turkey|solar power]] increasing [[energy independence]] and reducing import costs, but are not much interested in the climate benefits.<ref name=":14" /> The arts are raising awareness of climate change (although some are sponsored by companies whose environmental policies have been criticised<ref name=":14" />),<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-11-12|title=Turkey's Sertab raises climate change awareness with new song 🇹🇷|url=https://eurovision.tv/story/sertab-new-song|access-date=2021-12-08|website=Eurovision.tv|language=en-gb}}</ref> and [[Education in Turkey|education]] is supported by the EU.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2019-08-29|title=Turkey's stage-struck grannies act to save the planet|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/blogs-news-from-elsewhere-49496227|access-date=2019-09-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Enhancing Required Joint Efforts on Climate Action Project |url=http://www.iklimin.org/en/proje-hakkinda/}}</ref>  Protests against opencast coal mining, such as at [[Akbelen Forest]], have been covered by small media outlets such as ''Yeşil Gazete'' and ''Kaldıraç Magazine''.<ref name=":14" />

===Public perception===
[[File:20231129 Survey - I expect to be displaced by climate change - Ipsos.svg|thumb|2023 Survey - I expect to be displaced by climate change - Ipsos]]
[[Individual action on climate change]] is not properly understood (in a survey of primary school teachers many erroneously prioritised using less cosmetics) and neither are government choices on [[climate change mitigation]] (in the same survey only a minority correctly prioritised curbing fossil fuel use).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yalcin |first1=Fatma Aggul |last2=Yalcin |first2=Mehmet |title=Turkish Primary Science Teacher Candidates' Understandings of Global Warming and Ozone Layer Depletion |journal=Journal of Education and Training Studies |date=2017 |volume=5 |issue=10 |page=218 |doi=10.11114/jets.v5i10.2225 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Future warming of seawater by [[Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant]] is wrongly thought by some to be relevant to climate change.<ref name="TemaWWF">{{cite book|url=http://sertifika.tema.org.tr/_Ki/CevreKutuphanesi/Documents/Iklim-Degisiklik-Yerel-Etkileri-Rapor-Kitapcigi.pdf|title=İkli̇m Deği̇şi̇kli̇ği̇ni̇n Yerel Etki̇leri̇ Raporu|date=March 2015|publisher=[[Turkish Foundation for Combating Soil Erosion]] and WWF-Turkey|isbn=978-975-7169-77-2|language=tr|trans-title=Report on local effects of climate change|access-date=2018-10-11|archive-date=2019-03-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328230827/http://sertifika.tema.org.tr/_Ki/CevreKutuphanesi/Documents/Iklim-Degisiklik-Yerel-Etkileri-Rapor-Kitapcigi.pdf}}</ref>

İklim Haber (Climate News) and [[KONDA Research and Consultancy]] found in 2018 that over three-quarters of [[public opinion on climate change]] thinks that extreme weather has increased.<ref name="Website-5" /> Over 70% of the public acknowledge that current climate crisis is a result of human activities.<ref>{{Cite web|date=November 2020|title=Türki̇ye'de İkli̇m Deği̇şi̇kli̇ği̇ Ve Çevre Sorunları Algısı 2020|trans-title=2020 opinion about climate change and environmental issues in Turkey|url=https://www.iklimhaber.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/konda-arastirma-rapor-2020s.pdf|url-status=live|access-date=30 November 2020|website=İklim Haber|pages=12–18|language=tr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126080248/https://www.iklimhaber.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/konda-arastirma-rapor-2020s.pdf |archive-date=2020-11-26 }}</ref> Some construction companies have been accused of [[greenwashing]], advertising their buildings as environmentally friendly without obtaining any [[green building]] certificates.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Erden|first1=Oğulkan|last2=Erkartal|first2=Pınar ÖKTEM|date=2019-09-02|title=Greenwashing in Turkey: Sustainability as an Advertising Strategy in Architecture|url=https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/797896|journal=A+Arch Design International Journal of Architecture and Design|volume=5|issue=1|pages=1–13}}</ref>

In a 2019 [[E3G]] poll of six [[Belt and Road Initiative]] countries (including Turkey), solar was the most popular energy source and coal the least popular.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-04-25|title=Polling finds citizens in six belt and road countries want clean energy, not coal|url=https://e3g.wpengine.com/media-room/polling-citizens-six-belt-and-road-countries-want-clean-energy-not-coal/|access-date=2020-09-30|website=E3G}}</ref> Twenty-four Turkish cities committed to the Paris Agreement targets that year,<ref>{{Cite web|last=Schulz|first=Florence|date=2019-12-10|title=24 Turkish cities oppose Erdogan, support Paris Climate Agreement|url=https://www.euractiv.com/section/climate-environment/news/24-turkish-cities-oppose-erdogan-support-paris-climate-agreement/|access-date=2020-05-27|website=www.euractiv.com}}</ref> and the [[United Nations Development Programme]] partnered with the [[Turkish Basketball Federation]] in 2020 to raise public awareness of the fight against climate change.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Bringing sustainable development into play: UNDP teams up with basketball federation to raise awareness|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/bringing-sustainable-development-into-play-undp-teams-up-with-basketball-federation-to-raise-awareness-152160|access-date=2020-05-27|website=Hürriyet Daily News}}</ref> A 2020 study found that the level of public support for a potential carbon tax does not depend on whether the proceeds are used for mitigation and adaptation.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Uyduranoglu|first1=Ayse|last2=Ozturk|first2=Serda Selin|date=2020-10-20|title=Public support for carbon taxation in Turkey: drivers and barriers|journal=Climate Policy|volume=20|issue=9|pages=1175–1191|doi=10.1080/14693062.2020.1816887|bibcode=2020CliPo..20.1175U |issn=1469-3062|s2cid=222094247}}</ref> In 2023 a draft law was proposed including public information and adding climate change to [[education in Turkey]].<ref name=":1a">{{Cite web |title=Climate Law On Its Way In Türkiye - Climate Change - European Union |url=https://www.mondaq.com/turkey/climate-change/1388384/climate-law-on-its-way-in-t%C3%BCrkiye |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=www.mondaq.com |language=en}}</ref> In 2024 a climate [[Web portal|portal]] was created and Turkish citizens can log in to it.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Türkiye's first Climate Portal launched to accelerate climate action |url=https://www.undp.org/turkiye/press-releases/turkiyes-first-climate-portal-launched-accelerate-climate-action |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=UNDP |language=en}}</ref> Similar to global public opinion most Turks favour climate action.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1038/s41558-024-01925-3 | title=Globally representative evidence on the actual and perceived support for climate action | date=2024 | last1=Andre | first1=Peter | last2=Boneva | first2=Teodora | last3=Chopra | first3=Felix | last4=Falk | first4=Armin | journal=Nature Climate Change | volume=14 | issue=3 | pages=253–259 | bibcode=2024NatCC..14..253A | doi-access=free }}</ref>

=== International cooperation ===
[[File:Mediterranean_Climate_Change_Initiative_2.jpg|thumb|Turkish President [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] with other country leaders at a meeting of the Mediterranean Climate Change Initiative in 2010.]]
According to the [[Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources (Turkey)|Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources]], climate change is one of the world's biggest problems.<ref>{{cite web |title=Climate Change and International Negotiations |url=http://www.enerji.gov.tr/en-US/Pages/Climate-Change-and-International-Negotiations |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180928200850/http://www.enerji.gov.tr/en-US/Pages/Climate-Change-and-International-Negotiations |archive-date=28 September 2018 |access-date=28 September 2018 |publisher=[[Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources (Turkey)]]}}</ref> Turkey was the fifth-largest recipient of multilateral climate funds between 2013 and 2016, receiving $231 million through channels such as the [[Climate Investment Funds|Clean Technology Fund]] (CTF) and the [[Global Environment Facility]] (GEF).<ref name="CarbonBrief">{{cite web |date=3 May 2018 |title=The Carbon Brief Profile: Turkey |url=https://www.carbonbrief.org/carbon-brief-profile-turkey |access-date=1 October 2018 |website=Carbon Brief}}</ref>

In 2021, Turkey ratified the [[Paris Agreement]], with all parliamentary members voting to ratıfy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Turkey finally ratified the Paris Agreement. Why now? |url=https://www.mei.edu/publications/turkey-finally-ratified-paris-agreement-why-now |access-date=2021-12-02 |website=Middle East Institute |language=en}}</ref> Prior to this, it was one of the last few remaining countries, alongside neighboring country [[Iran]], to not have ratified the agreement. It was the last of the G20 countries to ratify. Their reason for delay, according to the current presidency at the [[2020 G20 Riyadh summit|G20 summit in 2020]], was the countries "negligible historical responsibility for greenhouse gas emissions (less than 1%)". Turkey is not party to the [[Convention on Environmental Impact Assessment in a Transboundary Context]] (Espoo Convention).<ref>{{Cite web |title=United Nations Treaty Collection |url=https://treaties.un.org/Pages/ViewDetails.aspx?src=TREATY&mtdsg_no=XXVII-4&chapter=27&lang=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210301045913/https://treaties.un.org/pages/ViewDetails.aspx?src=TREATY&mtdsg_no=XXVII-4&chapter=27&lang=en |archive-date=2021-03-01 |access-date=2020-10-11 |website=treaties.un.org}}</ref> In 2021 Turkey ratified the [[Kigali Amendment]] to reduce production and use of [[hydrofluorocarbon]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=United Nations Treaty Collection |url=https://treaties.un.org/pages/ViewDetails.aspx?src=IND&mtdsg_no=XXVII-2-f&chapter=27&clang=_en |access-date=2020-11-24 |website=treaties.un.org |language=EN}}</ref> [[Armenia]] says that dam construction in Turkey has combined with climate change to reduce flow in the [[Aras (river)|Araks River]] basin.<ref>{{cite news |date=23 March 2021 |title="Use every drop of water sparingly" –hydrometeorologist warns as Turkish dams and climate change cut resources |agency=[[Armenpress]] |url=https://armenpress.am/eng/news/1046870.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210324193926/https://armenpress.am/eng/news/1046870.html |archive-date=24 March 2021}}</ref> Turkey will host the [[2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference]].

Turkey sent over a thousand representatives to the [[2023 United Nations Climate Change Conference]] and joined various initiatives, such as decarbonizing cement production. However it was criticised for not voting to [[Fossil fuel phase-out|phase-out fossil fuels]], with Umit Şahin at [[Sabancı University]] Istanbul Policy Center saying that would be good for [[Economy of Turkey|the economy]] as Turkey is a fossil fuel importer.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-12-13 |title=COP28: Türkiye rekor sayıda temsilciyle katıldığı Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) İklim Değişikliği Konferansı'nda istediğini elde etti mi? |url=https://www.bbc.com/turkce/articles/c519y4wnz54o |access-date=2023-12-16 |website=BBC News Türkçe |language=tr}}</ref>
